subject.title: Stuck-session liveness monitor misclassifies healthy processing runs as stale during event-loop stalls

question: Should OpenClaw change the processing/no-activeWorkKind recovery policy now, or require live measurement proving that healthy active runs can lose activity bookkeeping during event-loop stalls?
rationale: Current source shows the reported fallthrough and existing tests depend on it, but the reported healthy-run abort chain is still source-plausible rather than confirmed by a current-main live reproduction.

options.title: Require proof first
options.body: Keep this issue open for a controlled log or deterministic harness reproduction showing state=processing, classification=stale_session_state, and an abort of a healthy active run before changing recovery semantics.

options.title: Patch classifier now
options.body: Approve a narrow change that prevents processing/no-activeWorkKind from immediate stale recovery, with replacement tests for genuine ownerless stale processing recovery.

options.title: Fold into liveness redesign
options.body: Treat this as part of the broader stuck-session recovery ladder and event-loop liveness work instead of changing this classifier edge alone.

recommendation.title: Require proof first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a controlled log or deterministic harness reproduction showing state=processing, classification=stale_session_state, and an abort of a healthy active run before changing recovery semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent ownerless-lane recovery work is closest to the policy boundary this issue would change.
